android-navigation|NavigationBar.summary: A Plenix navigation bar on Android is Material 3’s navigation bar, used for the top-level destinations of a multi-area app at Narrow (under 600 dp), kept native in behavior (one destination always selected, ripple, TalkBack tab semantics, font scaling, the gesture bar inset) and styled with the Plenix tokens: the default surface with a divider line along its top, 80 dp tall, 24 dp icons, DM Sans labels always shown, and the current destination in the Plenix selected colors. Material’s default is a tinted surface container with a secondary-container indicator; Plenix keeps Material’s structure and replaces the look.

/** A top-level destination: outlined icon, filled when current, and an optional count. */
data class Destination(val route: String, val label: String, val icon: ImageVector, val currentIcon: ImageVector, val count: Int = 0)
/** The Plenix navigation bar on Android: Material 3’s NavigationBar, styled with the generated Plenix tokens. */
fun PlenixNavigationBar(destinations: List<Destination>, current: String, onSelect: (Destination) -> Unit) {
val label = TextStyle(fontFamily = DmSans, fontSize = PlenixPlatform.textCaptionSize, lineHeight = PlenixPlatform.textCaptionLineHeight)
Icon(if (isCurrent) d.currentIcon else d.icon, contentDescription = null, Modifier.size(PlenixPlatform.navBarIconSize))
// In the app frame, under 600 dp (PlenixPlatform.shellPhoneBelow); the rail takes over from there
Scaffold(bottomBar = { PlenixNavigationBar(destinations, current = route, onSelect = { navController.navigate(it.route) }) }) { padding -> Content(padding) }

// Kotlin. Views take ARGB ints and pixels: a Plenix color for the current appearance, a Plenix dp in pixels
fun Context.argb(light: Color, dark: Color): Int =
(if ((resources.configuration.uiMode and Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_MASK) == Configuration.UI_MODE_NIGHT_YES) dark else light).toArgb()
fun Context.px(dp: Dp): Float = dp.value * resources.displayMetrics.density
